facts.content: Sudden severe left-sided headache with visual changes.
facts.source_text: CC: Sudden severe L-sided HA with visual changes

facts.content: Headache onset was 4 hours ago, abrupt, with a pain level of 6/10.
Associated symptoms include blurred vision with zig-zag lines, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting twice.
facts.source_text: Assoc: blurred vision w/ zig-zag lines, dizziness, N/V ×2

facts.content: Symptoms worsen with movement and there is screen intolerance.
Tried paracetamol 3 hours ago without relief.
facts.source_text: Tried paracetamol 3 h ago → no relief

facts.content: No limb weakness and gait is okay.
Patient is not on any medications.
Suspected migraine with aura versus other acute intracranial pathology.
facts.source_text: Suspected migraine w/ aura vs other acute intracranial pathology

facts.content: Nausea and vomiting related to headache.
Start ibuprofen 400 mg, OTC anti-emetic, sugary carbonated drink, and rest in a dark room.
facts.source_text: Start ibuprofen 400 mg + OTC anti-emetic + sugary carbonated drink; rest in dark room

facts.content: Attend same-day clinic appointment for full neurological exam, may cancel if symptoms resolve.
facts.source_text: Same-day clinic appt for full neuro exam; may cancel if symptoms resolve

facts.content: Educated on red flags such as increasing severity, neurological deficits, and persistent vomiting directing to A&E.

facts.content: Reassure and offer follow-up as needed.
